summary: Area blocklist (country / postcode prefix) feature tested end-to-end. Backend: 12/12 pytest pass. Tests cover POST area with no criteria → 400, prefix ' im ' stored as 'IM', GET returns kind/country/postcode_prefix with no _id, customer blocks still get kind='customer', delete then 404, admin auth required, checkout 403 with the area message for BT1 1AA, bt11aa, Ireland/D02 X285 and a billing address in BT, the customer-block message is kept separate, and a UK SW1A 1AA order succeeds. Frontend admin: the Blocklist tab shows area-block-form, both existing Ireland and BT rows have amber 'Area' badges and the BT row reads 'Postcodes starting BT'. Adding prefix 'im' turns it into IM, the row appears with a badge, and deleting it via unblock-{id} (confirm dialog) removes it; it stays gone after reload. The empty-form check shows a toast. Frontend guest checkout: BT1 1AA (UK) and D02 X285 (Ireland) both show the destructive toast 'Order not accepted — Sorry — we don't currently ship to this area…', the API returns 403, no order is created and the page stays on the details step. SW1A 1AA (UK) creates order GHP-078 and moves to the Payment step. The paylink address endpoint (PUT /api/orders/pay/{id}/address) was only code-reviewed: it uses the same find_block_match / blocked_message path. It was not run.

minor.issue: Uses entry_matches only, so area entries never flag existing orders. Orders already placed from BT or Ireland are not highlighted as blocked in the admin orders list. Use area_matches for kind=='area' as find_block_match does.

Country matches by substring (e_country in a_country). Blocking 'Niger' would also block 'Nigeria', and 'Ireland' also blocks 'Northern Ireland', which is probably intended but implicit. Prefix match is on the raw postcode start regardless of country, so a prefix like 'B' would also block BT, BA and so on. No problem with the current entries.
'kind' is not validated. Any value other than 'area' is silently treated as 'customer'. Consider Literal['customer','area'].

issues: The 'How blocking works' info box doesn't mention area blocks. Add a bullet about country / postcode-prefix blocks.
Tab label 'Blocked customers' now also holds area blocks; consider 'Blocklist'.

action_items: Optional: add data-testids to checkout address inputs, the country select and the 'Continue to payment' button (tests currently rely on #email, positional inputs and the button role/name)
Optional: validate kind as Literal and tighten country matching to exact match

record_hit on area entries overwrites last_hit_details with customer PII (name/email/postcode). That is fine, but no notification email is sent for area hits (by design)

Side effect: the hits counter / last_hit_at / last_hit_details on the existing BT (now 5) and Ireland (now 3) entries went up because of the blocked test attempts. The order counter also moved forward.
